# SOP-P3-L1-03 First-article inspection - Hot Forge line
Revision: Rev A
Plant: P3, line P3-L1
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03
Related documents: ECN-2026-006, MM-P3-L1-SB02, MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3

Purpose
1. This procedure defines the steps required to perform the first-article inspection for the Hot Forge line in P3-L1, verifying process readiness and part conformance prior to production release.

Background and rationale
2. First-article inspection validates the combined performance of induction heating, transfer, and forging systems and confirms material and tooling setup before full production. The critical control point for the heating subsystem is the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) which must reach 1260 °C. Achieving and documenting this target ensures consistent material flow and microstructure after forging and reduces the risk of downstream rework.

Scope
3. Applies to all first-article parts produced on P3-L1 using EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Does not replace routine in-process inspection requirements in MM-P3-L1-SB02 or maintenance directions in MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.

Preconditions
4. Verify the following before starting:
   - Engineering change notices affecting the part or tooling have been reviewed: ECN-2026-006.
   - Machine maintenance applicable to EQ-P3-L1-SB02 and EQ-P3-L1-HP01 has been completed per MM-P3-L1-SB02 and MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.
   - Tooling and dies installed are the approved configuration for the part number under review.
   - Lubrication for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) uses part number CFW-LUB-927.
   - Calibration status of measurement instruments is current and traceable.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
5. Mandatory PPE for all personnel in the hot forge area:
   - Heat-resistant gloves and arm guards.
   - Face shield with thermal protection.
   - Flame-retardant apron or jacket.
   - Safety footwear rated for impact and molten metal splash.
   - Hearing protection as required in the forge area.

Responsibilities
6. Operator: execute process steps and collect inspection data.
7. Quality inspector: perform dimensional and metallurgical checks, verify records.
8. Shift supervisor: authorize first-article approval or hold.
9. Maintenance: support adjustments and corrective action if equipment deviation occurs.

Procedure — numbered steps
10. Prepare the line
   10.1 Confirm preconditions and PPE per Sections 4 and 5.
   10.2 Verify tooling and die part numbers visually and against routing paperwork.
   10.3 Record ambient conditions and instrument identifiers on the first-article checklist.

11. Load and heat billet
   11.1 Confirm material identity and mill certifications match the job ticket.
   11.2 Load a billet into EQ-P3-L1-IH03 following standard transfer protocols for P3-L1.
   11.3 Initiate the induction heating cycle for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and monitor temperature controls.
   11.4 Verify the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C and record the measured value(s) and instrument ID on the checklist.
   Rationale: Reaching 1260 °C ensures the billet attains the required forging temperature window for material flow and metallurgical properties.

12. Transfer and pre-form inspection
   12.1 Transfer the heated billet to the transfer system EQ-P3-L1-SB02.
   12.2 Inspect the billet visually for surface condition, scale, and alignment prior to pressing.
   12.3 Confirm transfer timing and orientation meet die entry requirements and document any deviation.

13. Forge cycle and part capture
   13.1 Position billet in Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01).
   13.2 Ensure lubrication applied to tools is CFW-LUB-927 and document lot or batch identifier associated with the lubricant.
   13.3 Execute the first forge stroke(s) to produce the first-article part.
   13.4 Capture the part and record any observed issues during forming (flash distribution, die fill, surface defects).

14. Inspection and verification
   14.1 Perform dimensional measurements against engineering drawings and record results on the first-article inspection form.
   14.2 Conduct metallurgical checks required by the part specification and record sample IDs and results.
   14.3 If nonconformances are found, tag the part and initiate containment and notification per ECN-2026-006.

15. Examples and acceptance criteria
   15.1 Example documentation entries: list of dimensions measured, instrument serial numbers, temperature reading annotated as 1260 °C for EQ-P3-L1-IH03, lubricant lot tied to CFW-LUB-927.
   15.2 Acceptance is granted when dimensional and metallurgical results conform to the drawing, the temperature reading for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 is recorded as 1260 °C, and no critical process deviations are open.

Records to keep
16. Mandatory records to be retained in the document control system:
   - Completed first-article inspection checklist and signed copy.
   - Temperature log showing EQ-P3-L1-IH03 reading of 1260 °C.
   - Lubricant usage record specifying CFW-LUB-927 and batch/lot traceability.
   - Dimensional inspection sheets and metallurgical test reports.
   - Any related nonconformance reports and corrective actions referencing ECN-2026-006.

Deviations and corrective action
17. If the EQ-P3-L1-IH03 temperature does not reach 1260 °C or stability cannot be achieved, stop the first-article run and notify maintenance. Record the event and reference MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3 for maintenance escalation.

Sign-off
18. Signatures required before production release:
   18.1 Operator signature and date.
   18.2 Quality inspector signature and date.
   18.3 Shift supervisor signature and date authorizing release to production.

Appendix — references
19. Referenced documents: ECN-2026-006, MM-P3-L1-SB02, MM-P3-L1-SB02-S3.
